To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the moral support provided by family members and social capital are important determinants of women-owned business growth in the Islamic Republic.
women-owned businesses in Pakistan grow when women have the personal resources, social values and support of family members.
the growth of women entrepreneurs’ enterprises is influenced by the social values of their family, and by the Islamic traditions that allow women to meet with men and to have independent mobility.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how social values and Islamic tradition influence the growth of women entrepreneurs in Pakistan.
how women entrepreneurs in Pakistan use their entrepreneurial capital to overcome the barriers to their business growth.

how the entrepreneurial process is influenced by the social and cultural context of the society in which women entrepreneurs operate, and the extent to which the growth of womenowned enterprises in Pakistan is constrained by the social values and Islamic culture.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the growth of womenowned businesses is not only determined by the personal resources and social values of the women themselves but also by the Islamic traditions and the social values of the society at large.
social values and Islamic norms and traditions are the main determinants of women-owned enterprise growth.
the growth of women entrepreneurs in Pakistan is influenced by their personal resources, social capital and social values, and the Islamic tradition in which they operate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the growth of womenowned enterprises in Pakistan is a result of the interplay of the personal and social resources of the entrepreneur, the social and religious environment, and the support of the family and society.
women entrepreneurs’ entrepreneurial capital, social values, and Islamic traditions are significant variables in their growth and success.

women entrepreneurs’ social capital and personal resources have a significant role to play in their business growth in Pakistan, and this growth is positively affected by the moral support of their immediate family and independent mobility.
The main takeaway from our work is that
women’s social values and their religious traditions can be leveraged to promote women’s entrepreneurship.
the social values and traditions of an Islamic society can play a positive role in the development of female-owned businesses.
women entrepreneurs in Islamic societies are not only able to overcome the social barriers of their societies, but also to use their social networks and resources to grow their business.
